title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a computation. It is a handwritten programme list of conjectures, written on the blank verso of a Bourbaki typescript (n°357, p. 33, an integration draft whose text shows through in mirror image). It sits among Grothendieck's 'Cristaux (1970)' scribbles, after a page on the cohomological class of a smooth pair (Y,X) via the Kummer coboundary (SGA 4/5-style purity). The list reads roughly as follows, with marginal glosses on the right.

(1) 'Conj. de Hodge (crist., généralisée)'. Gloss: 'déc. de Hodge sur C' and 'opération de Galois, conj. Frobenius'. This is the crystalline/p-adic analogue of the Hodge conjecture, in the form Grothendieck sketched in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1966/68). Take X smooth proper over W (or a p-adic base) and a cycle class on the special fibre. Its crystalline class should come from an algebraic cycle on the lifting iff it lies in the appropriate step Fil^i of the Hodge filtration on H_dR(X_K). The gloss records the analogy: over C the extra structure is the Hodge decomposition; in arithmetic it is the Galois action or the Frobenius.

(2) 'Conj. de Tate (crist., généralisée)'. This is the crystalline Tate conjecture: classes in H^{2i}_cris⊗Q on which p^{-i}F acts by the identity should be algebraic. The 'generalized' version presumably covers the relative/variational case.

(3) 'Conj. des Frobenius dans Coh. de De Rham (à connexion)'. Gloss: 'Frobenius cristallins'. In a smooth family over a p-adic base, relative de Rham cohomology with its Gauss–Manin connection should carry a horizontal Frobenius structure, i.e. be an F-crystal. Questions then follow on the behaviour of this Frobenius, e.g. Newton versus Hodge (Katz's conjecture, proved by Mazur 1972-73) and its relation to Dwork's theory.

(4) '? Conj. du double réseau (revoir)'. I read this as the problem of comparing two integral lattices in one p-adic vector space. One lattice comes from étale/Tate-module data, the other from crystalline/de Rham (Dieudonné) data over a mixed-characteristic DVR. This is the integral side of Grothendieck's 'fonction mystérieuse' (ICM 1970, 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux'). The reading is plausible but not certain; the question mark and '(revoir)' show Grothendieck himself was unsure of the formulation.

(5) 'Tate gen[?] (crist., généralisé) sur schémas de t.f. sur Z / de t.f. sur corps'. This is Tate's conjecture in the generality of Tate's 1964 Woods Hole paper: orders of poles of zeta functions of schemes of finite type over Z or over a field versus ranks of cycle groups. Here it would be in a crystalline variant.

(6) 'Tate gen[?] sur anneaux locaux d'inégales car.'. This is a Tate-type statement over mixed-characteristic local rings. It is most naturally Tate's Hodge–Tate decomposition (Tate 1967, conjectured in general, proved by Faltings 1988), or a Tate-conjecture analogue for p-adic local bases. It matches the gloss 'déc. de Hodge sur C / opération de Galois'.

Overall the page is a to-do list for a crystalline programme parallel to the Hodge/Tate philosophy.
errors: No mathematical claims are proved, so there is nothing to check for correctness.
The word after 'Tate' on the last two lines is uncertain ('genus', 'gén.', 'géom.'?), so the exact intended statements of items (5) and (6) are conjectural.

missed.claim: Grothendieck lists a 'conjecture du double réseau' among his crystalline conjectures. It is apparently a comparison of two integral lattices (étale versus crystalline/de Rham) in mixed characteristic. He flagged it himself as needing revision, and the name does not seem to circulate in the literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early hint that Grothendieck envisaged an integral comparison, beyond the rational 'fonction mystérieuse'. Such a comparison was achieved only much later (Fontaine–Laffaille, Breuil–Kisin, Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze). It is of historical interest for dating the integral question; the content is too sketchy to be a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a programme list of known (or soon-to-be-known) crystalline analogues of the Hodge and Tate conjectures, consistent with Grothendieck's 1966-70 published remarks. The only mildly notable item is the named, unexplained 'double lattice' conjecture.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 right-margin gloss reads 'déc. de Hodge sur C' / 'opération de Galois, conj. Frobenius' (as transcribed); the parenthesis on lines 1–2 is '(Crist., généralisée)'.
The word read as 'genus' on the last two lines is uncertain; possibly 'gén.' (généralisé) or 'géom.'. The last line reads 'sur anneaux locaux d'inégales car.'.
The faint mirror-image typed text is the Bourbaki integration typescript (n°357, p. 33) bleeding through from the other side, not part of the notes.
